_doc: Campaign shell (M5): one region strip — nodes unlock in order, each is an encounter from enemies.json; winning holds the node, granting income per real-world day (timestamp-computed) and notoriety. Notoriety crossing threatGen2At announces Threat Generation 2 and unlocks nodes gated with 'threatGen': 2. rescueEncounter = the themed battle used for every rescue raid (v0.1 has one template). Adding regions/nodes must never require engine edits. unlocksFauna: species ids added to the Mail-Order catalog when the node is held. Region contestation (§3.9 'coalition counter-offensives can contest held regions'): once the threat generation named in `contestation.startsAtGen` is reached, the coalition periodically comes BACK for a node you already hold. The schedule is a timestamp (nextContestAt), never a per-tick dice roll, so how often you open the app cannot change how often you are attacked; and the defence window starts the moment you SEE the contest, so being away never costs you a node you were never given the chance to defend. Adding a region must never require engine edits, and neither does tuning this.

contestation._doc: startsAtGen/minHeld gate the whole system so early play is untouched. cooldownHours is the gap between counter-offensives, lengthened by cooldownPerDefenceHours for every successful defence of that node — they learn. windowHours is how long you have once you see it. The defence reuses the node's OWN encounter at `escalation` above its authored strength, growing by escalationPerDefence every time you hold the place: a continuous dial rather than a tier step, because the authored tier ladder is deliberately lumpy (a tier is a band of CONTENT) and +1 tier on an already-top-tier boss is a wall while +1 on a mid encounter is a shrug. A new region therefore costs zero new encounter data, and the ramp is endless and self-paced. rewardScale multiplies the node encounter's reward; holding the line also impounds one of the attacking units, because a conquest reward has to expand what you can CREATE (Law 2) and enemy tech is how this one does. Measured against the balance harness's yardstick team of three at prismatic: a first defence runs 100/98/88/12/42% across the five Greenfield nodes against 100/100/93/30/55% for the original assault.
contestation.blurb: They have been back to the drawing board and the drawing board had a bigger budget.
contestation.intel: Counter-offensive: the same garrison at {pct}% strength. They have held a grudge and, worse, a budget.

news.opened: COUNTER-OFFENSIVE: a convoy is rolling on {node}. Revenue suspended pending, quote, "the situation."
news.held: {node} holds. The convoy reverses at speed and one vehicle does not reverse at all.
news.lost: {node} has been retaken by the coalition. They have already put up a sign about it. You can take it back.
news.expired: {node} was abandoned without a shot. The coalition is describing this as a victory and, annoyingly, it is.
